# Inbound title is reverted by outbound local-wins, so a Jira-side summary edit never reaches the local ticket

## Symptom

Live against the Jira Data Center harness (run 30724309686),
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_mutation_round_trips[02-edit-summary]`
fails: a DC summary edit, confirmed present in the JQL index, does not reach the bound local
ticket's `.title` after a clean writing pass. The sibling `[03-edit-description]` PASSES on the
same fixture and the same pass, as do add/remove-label, comment, assign and unassign. The
failure is title-specific.

## Proven root cause

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py:38-45` defined the arbitration set as
`_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS = frozenset({"description", "priority", "status", "assignee"})` and its
comment declared `title` "deliberately absent", on the grounds that the pre-625b differ iterated
Jira-shaped keys (whose title key is `summary`, never a member of the local-named set) so title
was never suppressed, and that behaviour was preserved verbatim.

The guard `_suppressed_by_inbound` (`outbound_field_diff.py:247-256`) is membership-gated on that
set, and the title comparison at `outbound_field_diff.py:265-268` sat OUTSIDE every guard. So when
a teammate edits the Jira summary while local is unchanged since the baseline, the outbound differ
emits `title = <stale local value>`. The inbound differ then DROPS its own correct title update as
a contradiction of a just-emitted outbound change for the same target: `inbound_differ.py:483-486`
maps outbound `summary` to inbound `title`, and `inbound_differ.py:653-656` filters it out
(bidirectional suppression, bug 3bf8).

Two consequences, only the first of which the live cell observed:

1. the Jira-side title never reaches the local ticket; and
2. the stale local title is pushed back over the Jira edit.

## Why description passes and title does not

`description` IS in the set, the fixture's local description equals the baseline, so
`_suppressed_by_inbound` returns True, no outbound description is emitted, and the inbound
description flows. That is the whole asymmetry.

## Authority violated

`docs/adr/0026-reconciler-three-way-merge-baseline.md:21-31` names the arbitrated set as "the five
inbound-mirrored scalar fields (title/description/priority/status/assignee)" and mandates: local ==
baseline means the outbound push is SUPPRESSED so the inbound differ mirrors it; local != baseline
means local-wins. `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:269` documents Title as syncing Jira to Local. Not
DC-specific: the module is vendor-neutral, so Cloud reverts a Jira-side summary edit identically.

## Runtime proof

Driving `diff_canonical_fields` directly with local title == baseline title and a differing remote
title returned `{'title': 'OLD'}`; the same call with description varied instead returned `{}`.
Feeding that outbound emission into `compute_inbound_mutations` returned `[]` with
`suppression_count == 1`, versus `[{'title': 'NEW-from-jira'}]` with no outbound context.

## Acceptance criteria

- With a baseline carrying `title` and local `title` matching it, a differing remote title emits NO
  outbound `title`; the inbound differ mirrors it into the local ticket.
- local `title` != baseline `title` still emits local-wins outbound (unchanged).
- No baseline, or a baseline omitting `title`, still degrades to local-wins (unchanged).
- A unit test on the LIVE canonical path (`outbound_field_diff`), not on the production-dead
  `adapters/jira/outbound_fields._diff_fields`.
